title: Still early, but the shape is showing
dek: Coinbase price, Farside ETF flows, and OKX positioning through the 23 September long-liquidation wave.
thesis: The shape is showing; the tail is not confirmed.
stakes: The $87.4k squeeze produced a long flush below $84k. The next evidence is whether $82k/$80k holds while flow and leverage reset.
subscribeHook: When $82k holds — or $77k fails — the letter updates the sequence. Charts stay free here; the call moves by email.
sourceNote: Issue 26 charts use Coinbase Exchange UTC candles, Farside Investors US-session ETF flows, and OKX public BTC-USDT perpetual open-interest/funding data. The 23 September ETF row is marked preliminary; weekend blanks are not zeroes. Educational scenario research; no leverage.

briefs.headline: The rejection did not erase the recovery
briefs.lede: A 4.3% high-to-low day is serious; it is not yet a break of the inherited $77k gate.
briefs.bodyHtml:
Fact. Coinbase's 23 September candle reached $87,283, traded to $83,513, and closed at $84,378.

Read. The next doors are $82–83k, $80k, and $77k. A severe tail requires those structures to fail in sequence.

briefs.headline: Flows helped, but the latest row is incomplete
briefs.lede: Reported ETF creations are supportive; the 23 September cells do not yet prove a persistent cash bid.
briefs.bodyHtml:
Fact. Farside reported +$999.0M on 21 September and +$714.7M on 22 September. The 23 September table showed +$32.4M with several issuer cells blank.

Read. Supportive is observable. Persistent is still a hypothesis.

briefs.headline: OI came out, but not back to baseline
briefs.lede: The rally rebuilt leverage; the 23 September flush released some of it without resetting the whole venue.
briefs.bodyHtml:
Fact. OKX BTC-USDT perpetual OI rose from $2.14B on 15 September to $2.66B on 20 September, then fell to $2.48B on 23 September.

Read. This is a venue-specific reset. It is not evidence that the market is either fully clean or definitely doomed.
